title: Finite and countable sets: counting, enumeration, and examples
summary: Count finite sets, enumerate integers and rationals, and prove that subsets, images, finite unions, and finite products of countable sets are countable.
abstract: A bijection lets us count a set without depending on the names of its elements. We first justify finite counting and the pigeonhole principle, then distinguish finite lists from infinite enumerations. Encodings by natural numbers explain how to handle repetitions and why familiar constructions preserve countability. A diagonal enumeration of pairs leads to a list containing every rational number.
